summary: This proposed standard defines managed objects that describe the behavior of an SNMPv2 entity itself. It was replaced by RFC 1907.

plainLanguage.summary: This paper lists what a network manager can ask about the management software on a device, rather than about the device itself.

subtitle: Management objects for SNMP v2 network management entities

tldr.problem: SNMP v2 entities need standardized ways to report their own internal state and events, including error counters, message handling statistics, and trap configuration.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 1450 defines managed objects in ASN.1 that describe the behavior of an SNMPv2 entity itself, organized into groups for statistics, object resources, traps, and conformance.
tldr.outcome: Network managers can monitor how their SNMP agents are performing. RFC 1907 replaced this specification with updated definitions for the SNMPv2 MIB.

facts.label: Groups defined
facts.value: SNMPv2 statistics, SNMPv1 statistics, object resources, traps, set, conformance

today: RFC 1450 was superseded by RFC 1907, which updated the SNMPv2 MIB definitions. RFC 1907 is the current standard for SNMPv2 MIB objects.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content:
A network management system consists of network nodes running management agents, management stations that monitor and control those agents, and a management protocol (SNMPv2) to exchange information. RFC 1450 defines managed objects that describe the behavior of a SNMPv2 entity itself, written in ASN.1 using the Structure of Management Information (SMI).

These managed objects, organized in the SNMPv2-MIB module, let network managers query and understand the internal state of SNMP agents on the network. The objects are organized into groups: SNMPv2 and SNMPv1 statistics, object resources, traps, and conformance information.
sections.plainLanguage: This standard defines what questions a network manager can ask about the SNMP software itself, not about the devices it manages.

sections.title: Statistics Groups
sections.content:
The SNMPv2 statistics group provides counters for basic instrumentation of the SNMPv2 entity. It tracks the total number of packets received, encoding errors, authentication failures, messages with bad operations, and messages that were silently dropped due to size constraints.

The SNMPv1 compatibility group provides additional counters for SNMPv2 entities that also implement SNMPv1. It counts SNMPv1 messages with unknown community names and unauthorized operations. These statistics help administrators diagnose connectivity issues and security problems in their SNMP deployments.
sections.plainLanguage: The statistics group keeps count of how many messages arrived, how many had errors, and why some messages were rejected or dropped.

sections.title: Object Resources and Traps
sections.content:
The Object Resource group allows an SNMPv2 entity acting as an agent to describe dynamically-configurable object resources. It includes a table that lists the object resources available on the agent and when they last changed. Not all SNMPv2 entities support dynamic configuration, so this group may be empty on some devices.

The Traps group manages notification configuration. It allows the SNMPv2 entity to be configured to generate SNMP traps, track which traps have been sent to each management entity, and record the number of traps sent to each destination. This enables managers to verify that notification delivery is working correctly.
sections.plainLanguage: One group describes what management objects the device knows about, and another group tracks notifications (traps) sent to network managers to alert them of problems.

sections.title: Compliance and Conformance
sections.content:
RFC 1450 includes conformance information specifying which parts of the MIB must be implemented. Compliance statements describe which groups of managed objects are required or optional for different types of SNMPv2 implementations. Units of conformance organize the objects into logical groups that implementations can support independently.

This allows implementations to declare what parts of the MIB they support, so managers know which objects they can safely query on a particular agent. Different device types (agents, managers, proxies) have different conformance requirements.
sections.plainLanguage: The standard says which information an SNMPv2 agent must provide and which is optional, so managers know what to expect from different types of devices.

sections.title: Relationship to Other Standards
sections.content:
RFC 1450 defines the SNMPv2 MIB based on the SMI framework defined in RFC 1902 (also known as SNMPv2-SMI). It imports definitions from RFC 1213 (MIB-II) and other standards, including the SNMPv2 party MIB for authentication and privacy configuration. The objects are defined using textual conventions from SNMPv2-TC.

This MIB works alongside other SNMPv2 standards: RFC 1901 defines the message format and protocol, RFC 1905 defines the protocol operations, and RFC 1906 defines the transport mappings. RFC 1907 superseded RFC 1450 with an updated SNMPv2 MIB.
sections.plainLanguage: This standard builds on other SNMP standards and defines the management objects in a standardized way using ASN.1 notation.
